prompt: A teacher quizzes her class five minutes after teaching a topic and the average score is 92%, so she records the topic as learned and schedules no further practice on it. Three weeks later, an end-of-unit test with questions of similar difficulty on the same topic averages 54%. The class was not re-taught the topic in between. What is the best interpretation of the two scores?

options.text: The class must have stopped trying on the second test, because a 92% average proves the learning was secure
The first quiz was probably marked too generously, and re-marking it would close most of the gap between the scores
The topic was learned well but is the kind of material that can only ever be recalled on the day it is taught

A quiz taken minutes after teaching mainly measures what is still fresh in mind, not durable retention; only a delayed, closed-book check after a gap would show what was really retained and what needs review

explanation: Performance straight after teaching overstates long-term learning, because the material has barely begun to be forgotten. A retrieval check delayed by days or weeks gives a far more honest picture of retention and tells the teacher which topics need spaced review before the final test.
